prerequisites: It is recommended for all students who have not studied Chemistry in the 2nd year of Bachillerato (high school) to complete the online Zero Chemistry courses provided by URJC to all its students to be able to pass the subject.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to understand and apply the principles of basic knowledge of general chemistry, organic and inorganic chemistry and their applications in engineering.

syllabus_topics: Atomic mass, atomic number, mass number and isotopes
Concept of mole and Avogadro's number
Secondary, consecutive, simultaneous reactions and overall reaction
Intermolecular or Van der Waals forces.
Real gases. Van der Waals equation.
Relationship between internal energy, heat and work.
Spontaneity of physical and chemical changes: Gibbs energy.
Calculation of equilibrium constants and equilibrium concentrations.
Dissociation of water. pH scale. pH measurement.
Potential and Gibbs Energy. Nernst Equation.
Non-spontaneous Redox processes. Electrolysis and Faraday's laws.

assessment_methods.method: Written test 1 (P1): theoretical questions, practical cases or problems (Block I)
Written test 2 (P2): theoretical questions, practical cases or problems (Block II)
Laboratory Practicals (PL): attendance, task execution, reports, test, observation
Case study 1 (EC1): attendance, short questions, report, observation (Block I)
Case study 2 (EC2): attendance, short questions, report, observation (Block II)

assessment_rules: The final grade (CF) is calculated as CF = P1 * 0.3 + P2 * 0.3 + PL * 0.2 + EC1 * 0.10 + EC2 * 0.10. To pass the course, CF must be >= 5, with minimum grades of P1 >= 4.5, P2 >= 4.5, PL >= 5, and an average of (P1 + P2)/2 >= 5. Students who do not pass in the ordinary call can re-take only the re-evaluable assessment activities (P1, P2, and parts of PL) in the extraordinary call. Mandatory attendance of 80% for classes and 100% for laboratory practicals is required to pass the course.
